name: PT Golden Eagle Energy Tbk

frontmatter.title: Golden Eagle Energy — a low-grade, long-haul thermal producer priced past its cycle
frontmatter.summary: Golden Eagle Energy is a small Indonesian thermal-coal producer whose coal is sub-bituminous and whose mine sits a long road haul from the river terminal, so its realised price is a fraction of the seaborne benchmark and its cash margin is thin. The share has re-rated far ahead of the economics on a thin free float. We initiate at SELL: our through-cycle value sits far below the market price.
thesis: We initiate at SELL with a target of Rp275 against a price of Rp3,280, a total return of -90.7%.

The variant view is grade and logistics, not price direction: Triaryani's coal is a sub-bituminous product around 4,100 kcal/kg GAR whose realised price has run at roughly a third of the Newcastle marker, and the road haul to the Lalan terminal is the single largest cost line in the P&L [S3] [S2].

At the coal deck's through-cycle Newcastle marker the mine's cash margin is a handful of dollars a tonne, so free cash flow is close to zero even after we strip the development capex out of the run rate [S3].
The market is not paying for through-cycle cash flow; today's price requires the seaborne benchmark to run far above the deck's forward path to be justified [S0].

The bull case is real and we state it: a sustained war-premium bid in seaborne coal, a lifted RKAB quota, a renewal of the mine licence past the end of the decade and the associate's idle East Kalimantan mine restarting would together change the arithmetic [S6].

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Golden Eagle Energy Tbk (SMMT) at **SELL** with a twelve-month target of **Rp275** versus a last price of Rp3,280, a total return of -90.7%. The company is a small Indonesian thermal-coal producer that sells a sub-bituminous product from one operating concession in South Sumatra and holds an indirect minority in a second mine in East Kalimantan that is operating but idle this year [S2] [S6]. Its coal is low-rank and its mine is a long road haul from the barging terminal, so its realised price ran at roughly a third of the Newcastle benchmark in the last audited year and its cost base is dominated by haulage, barging and jetty handling rather than by the coal-getting itself [S3] [S2]. The company has just re-rated sharply: the shares rose by roughly three-quarters in the month to end-September 2026, the exchange flagged unusual market activity and then suspended trading for cooling down, and management's own incidental public expose attributes the move mainly to transaction volume and to the index price rather than to a change in the business [S5] [S6].

Our variant view is not about the coal price. It is that the market is capitalising this asset on the seaborne benchmark while the company's own realised price is a small fraction of it, and that the mine's through-cycle cash margin is thin enough that free cash flow is close to zero even after we remove the one-off development spend that inflated the last two years' capex [S3]. Working from the coal deck's reviewed through-cycle marker, the calibrated realisation and the rate the accounts show being paid in royalty, the life-of-asset DCF is worth only Rp138 against today's price. The three things that move the value are the seaborne benchmark path, the annual RKAB quota that caps volume, and the haulage cost per tonne — the last of which the company has been investing to relieve through its Lalan river terminal and its own barge ports [S2].

We are not bearish by default. The bull case is explicit and is carried in the scenarios: a sustained war-premium bid in seaborne thermal coal, an RKAB quota lifted toward the company's own plan, and the restart of the associate's East Kalimantan mine would all lift volume and realised price together. A reader who believes the benchmark stays near spot rather than reverting to the deck should own this name; a reader who believes the deck should not.

Golden Eagle Energy began life as an entertainment company and only moved into coal mining in this
century, taking over a South Sumatran concession that has been producing since the middle of the
last decade. It is controlled by a Singapore-listed coal group whose regional office sits in
Jakarta, and its shares carry a very small free float, which makes the tape thin and prone to large
moves on modest flow. Sub-bituminous Indonesian coal of this rank is sold mainly to power stations
and cement plants in Asia, so demand tracks electricity generation and industrial activity rather
than the steel cycle.

Golden Eagle Energy is a coal-mining holding company. Its product reaches the market through PT Triaryani, a wholly-owned subsidiary that holds an IUP Operasi Produksi over a concession in the Musi Rawas Utara regency of South Sumatra and has been operating since the middle of the last decade [S2]. A second mine, PT Internasional Prima Coal in Palaran, East Kalimantan, is held as a forty-nine per cent associate through PT Mega Raya Kusuma and is therefore equity-accounted rather than consolidated [S2] [S6]. That distinction matters for anyone modelling the group: the income statement carries only Triaryani's revenue, while the group's headline operating statistics in the annual report include the associate's tonnes [S2]. The associate is not a shell: it is an operating mine with a higher-rank product than Triaryani's, holding an IUP over a large concession in East Kalimantan with its own haul road and barging ports [S2]. It produced 0.7 Mt Mt and sold 0.7 Mt Mt in the last audited year and sold close to a million tonnes the year before, and it paid the group US$2.1m of cash dividends in the last audited year [S2] [S3]. What it is is idle: it produced nothing at all in the current year while its licence ran down, and management blames the associate's absence for part of the group's output decline [S6]. So it is a real, cash-generative asset that is switched off, not a dormant one, and we value it at its carrying value only — its restart is upside we hold out of the base case [S3].

The product is thermal coal, and its rank is the heart of the investment case. Triaryani's coal carries a calorific value of about 4,100 kcal/kg GAR with low sulphur and low ash, and the company's own public-expose material describes the product as clean and homogeneous at a rank in the low four-thousands [S2] [S6]. The associate's coal is a materially higher-rank product [S2]. Both are open-pit operations; the group reports a single reportable segment, coal mining, and a single geographic area, Indonesia, so there is no segment split to manage [S3].

Strategically the company is a capacity builder rather than a consolidator. Its stated levers are to raise the production target inside the annual work plan and budget while respecting the logistics constraint of its coal haul road, to add haulage fleet and improve port loading, and to widen its market through long-term contracts while protecting coal quality to hold the selling price [S2]. The haulage route is the binding constraint: coal travels by road to a terminal on the Lalan river and then barges out, and the company has been adding road, jetty and barge-port infrastructure rather than buying tonnes [S2]. Management has also been restructuring the group's holding chain, moving its stake in the associate through a holding vehicle and buying the remaining interest in one of its intermediate holding companies in the last audited year [S3] [S6].

On competitive position the company is a challenger, not a leader. Its concession is small against the state producer or the large private coal names, it reports a single mine's worth of reserves rather than a portfolio, and it has no metallurgical coal, no downstream smelter and no branded product [S2]. The group employed a small workforce at the last count and has no institutionally-held float to speak of, with public shareholders holding a low-double-digit share of the register and the controlling shareholder holding the balance [S0].

Indonesian thermal coal is a mature, policy-shaped export industry. National production fell in the last completed year, the government's own reference price for high-calorie coal fell by roughly a fifth across that year, and the director general's published expectation for the coming year's national production target is lower again on softer demand from the main export destinations [S2]. Domestic consumption takes a large slice of national output through the domestic market obligation, with the balance exported or carried into stock [S2]. For a producer of this size, the binding constraints are therefore not market share but the annual government work plan and budget, known as the RKAB, which caps how much a concession may produce, and the US dollar reference prices the government sets twice a month [S2] [S6].

The coal deck is the driver we underwrite against. Its reviewed marker for high-rank seaborne thermal coal is a forecast path that starts above the last realised year, steps down through the middle of the decade and settles at a long-run level, with the deck explicitly flagging that spot sits well above the forward path as a war-premium carry rather than a level it expects to persist US$137/t US$118/t US$105/t. The government's own high-calorie reference price and the domestic power cap bracket the product set, and the deck's lower-rank reference prices for mid- and low-calorie grades show how steeply value declines with rank US$127/t US$70.0/t US$66.1/t. The deck's read on Indonesia's supply discipline and the demand outlook is the backdrop we work to [S2].

That grade ladder is our whole competitive read. A producer at the top of the rank ladder can realise close to the seaborne benchmark; a producer at Triaryani's rank realises a fraction of it, and then hands a further slice of the delivered price to the road haul, the barge, the jetty and the transshipment step before the coal reaches a vessel [S3]. Coal of this rank also competes with domestic mine-mouth supply for the power plants, and the domestic market obligation caps what those tonnes can earn at the government's power price rather than at export parity [S2].

On the five forces, buyer concentration is the practical constraint: a very large share of group revenue is a sale to a single related party within the controlling shareholder's group, under a coal sales and purchase agreement alongside a marketing-services agreement with the same counterparty [S3]. Suppliers are fewer than they look, because much of the cost base is contracted haulage and barging rather than a competitive commodity input [S3]. Related-party gravity runs through the cost side as well as the revenue side, and round one understated it. The logistics that carry the largest cost line — the haul road and the jetty — are provided by PT Marga Bara Jaya, an affiliate of the same controlling group, and the group funds that build through advances booked as other non-current assets [S3 note 17, note 34]. On the accounts' own cost-of-sales split, hauling is US$48.0m and jetty and loading a further US$8.0m [S3 note 28], together the majority of the cost of sales, so a large part of the cost base is contracted with an entity inside the controlling shareholder's group. Read the other way, the marketing-services fee the same group charges on the sales side, US$1.8m, is under a dollar a tonne off the realised price [S3 note 29, note 34]. We are precise about what is disclosed and what is not: the filing does not name the counterparty of the haulage charge line itself, and the one supplier it discloses above a tenth of sales is a third party [S3 note 28], so the related-party cost exposure is real but cannot be sized to the last dollar from the notes. A member of the board is also the president director of that logistics affiliate, which we note as a governance fact rather than a financing one [S2]. Barriers to entry are high on paper, since mining permits are not freely available, but they protect an incumbent that is still subscale and high-cost, which is a weak moat in practice [S2]. Substitution risk over the long run comes from the energy transition, which the company itself flags as its central sustainability challenge, and from the electrification of the mine fleet it says it is exploring [S2]. Regulation is the swing force: royalties, the domestic market obligation, export-proceeds retention rules and the frequency with which the RKAB quota is reset all move the economics of a marginal tonne more than they move a first-quartile one [S2] [S6].

The last audited year was a year of growth with almost no margin. Consolidated revenue doubled, but cost of sales rose by nearly the same amount, so gross profit was only a thin slice of sales and operating profit was marginal once general and administrative costs were taken 103.6 95.2 8.4 4.3. Reported net profit was small but larger than operating profit, because the group's share of the associate's earnings, a foreign-exchange gain and interest income all sat below the operating line [S3]. The cost of sales note is the most revealing page in the filing: haulage alone is the largest line, followed by barging, overburden removal, jetty and loading, then depreciation and amortisation, then the government royalty [S3]. Coal-getting proper is a minor item. This is a logistics business with a mine attached.

Volume is the swing factor, and the reported series is volatile. Triaryani sold roughly a million tonnes two years ago, then around two and a half million in the last audited year, and the company's own plan for the current year names a volume target well above that, paired with a revenue target that implies a materially higher realised price [S2]. We do not carry that plan into the base case, but not on the grounds round one used. Round one justified the gap with the claim that the company "met its own published plans at only a majority-of-target rate in each year it discloses"; that is only half supported and its locator was wrong. The annual report states in one place that the last audited year's production plan was met at 65.0% of the target set at the start of the year [S2], while its own structured target table shows the same year's sales target for Triaryani met at 2.5 Mt Mt against 2.6 Mt Mt actually sold — the target was reached, not missed [S2]. Two figures in one document, so we refuse to lean on either. The base case instead anchors on the hard print: group sales of 1.3 Mt Mt in the first half with no production at all from the associate, blamed on a work-plan quota issued only at the end of March [S4] [S6]. Annualising that run-rate and allowing a modest second-half recovery gives 2.7 Mt, rising only to 2.9 Mt and 3.0 Mt on paper — still below the last audited year's group total, and inside the logistics capacity the company itself describes [S2] [S6].

Realisation is the second swing factor and the one the market seems to ignore. We calibrate it on the last actual rather than on a forecast year, dividing the realised consolidated price by the benchmark's own average for the same year, so the ratio carries Triaryani's rank discount and its delivered-logistics point without any additional haircut 0.4 103.6 2.6 [S3] [S2]. That ratio, applied to the deck's through-cycle marker, is what produces a through-cycle realised price in the high thirties of dollars per tonne 39.1.

On costs we hold the mining rate, the other cash cost per tonne and the D&A rate at the last actual in real terms 31.9 28.6 2.1. The strip ratio is taken from the disclosed overburden volume against production and held flat, because nothing in the filing shows a mine plan with stripping drift 2.9 7,130,388 BCM. Royalty is set at the effective rate the accounts show being paid rather than at the tiered schedule, because the paid rate is stable across the last two audited years and the schedule's bands bracket it rather than match it 0.1 [S3].

The data pack's depreciation figure is the direct-method cash-flow artefact the house warns about, so we restate it from the cost-of-sales note; the restatement multiplies the reported charge by an order of magnitude and is what makes the reported EBITDA comparable with the cash margin [S3]. On capex we deliberately do not carry the last audited year's total into perpetuity. That total is dominated by additions to the stripping activity asset, exploration and evaluation assets and mining properties, which is a mine-development programme together with the one-off terminal and road build, so we hold the sustaining rate at the depreciation rate and treat the balance as development 2.1 [S3] [S2]. We flag the soft spot honestly: the depreciation charge that sets that rate fell by half between the last two audited years, and the notes do not explain the step, so the sustaining rate is a proxy rather than a mine plan [S3]. What the modelled volume step does not need is a new mine. The company's own strategy is to raise the output target inside the existing logistics capacity, so the incremental tonnes ride on fleet and on the annual quota rather than on plant [S2], and the capital actually spent on the haul road, jetty and ports sits as an advance to the logistics affiliate in other non-current assets, not in the capex line at all [S3 note 17]. If the last audited year's development rate were instead the true steady-state rate, free cash flow would thin further in every forecast year, so our sustaining assumption is if anything the more generous reading.

The balance sheet is levered to the controlling shareholder rather than to banks. Total debt at the last audited date is a non-current shareholder loan, drawn for the first time that year, and the group carried almost no bank debt before it 27.3 USD m [S3]. Liquidity is adequate but not comfortable, and operating cash flow has not covered capital expenditure for two years running, so the group has funded itself through a share placement and shareholder borrowing rather than through internally generated cash [S3]. Working capital is a modest negative, reflecting contract liabilities from customer advances and payable balances, and the restatement of D&A does not disturb it -2.9.

Earnings quality. The three-year accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets — is a small negative, roughly minus two-and-a-half per cent, and the year-to-year mix is noisy, so there is no accruals flag here; the volatile element is capitalised stripping and exploration, both legitimate in this industry and disclosed, so we classify them as optics-class rather than manipulation-class [S3] [S0]. The genuine quality issues are structural rather than accounting: related- party concentration on both sides of the P&L, the reliance on shareholder funding, and the volatility of the reported volume series against the smoothness of management's plans [S3] [S2]. On the cost side that concentration is the hauling and jetty logistics routed through the controlling group's affiliate and the marketing fee on the sale side, both set out in the industry section above [S3 note 17, note 29, note 34]. Two more structure points belong here rather than in a footnote. First, the associate is carried above its share of its own net assets — the group's US$25.4m carrying value against a forty-nine per cent share of the associate's US$31.1m of net assets — so an impairment test, not a write-up, is the direction of risk [S3]. Second, the group spent US$41.3m in cash last year buying an intermediate holding company from a counterparty the notes do not list as a related party, part-funded by a placement struck well below today's price [S3] [S2]. The audit is by a firm inside a global network, the opinion is clean, the accounts are in the US dollar, and we found no going-concern language, no special-notation status and no material litigation beyond a nominal administrative sanction for a late auditor appointment [S2] [S3].

The method set is the house coal card: a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices as the primary method, with an EV/EBITDA cross-check and a dividend-capacity cross-check, exactly as the industry card prescribes. A cyclical producer should never be valued on spot earnings or on a current-year multiple, because the current-year multiple embeds the wrong price; the deck's through-cycle marker is the sourced price we underwrite to, and the through-cycle marker is the anchor the whole valuation hangs from.

The cost of capital is built from the macro deck: a US dollar risk-free rate, a mature-market equity risk premium, an Indonesia country risk premium, an unlevered beta, and a small debt weight from the shareholder loan

. Because the company reports in US dollars, no currency premium is added twice; the source of return is the equity risk premium plus the country premium, geared by a levered beta that is barely above the unlevered one because the balance sheet is lightly geared 10.3% 0.83 10.6%.

The primary method discounts the free cash flow to the firm over the licensed window with no terminal value, so the value is the cumulative discounted cash the asset can generate while it is permitted to run

. Round one ran this DCF for twenty years to the middle of the next decade while citing a licence that expires at the end of this one, and the red team was right to call it: the horizon now stops where the licence stops. The operating permit for the producing mine expires in 2030 and the associate's in 2026, so the base case discounts five years of cash and nothing after 314 Mt [S2]. The reserve is far larger than that window — hundreds of millions of tonnes against a single-digit-million-tonne annual run-rate — but the filing carries no renewal term, so post-2030 cash is unpermitted upside, held out of base value and carried in the bull case the way this house treats exploration. That choice matters: stretching the horizon back to the reserve life would lift the primary value materially, and it is the single largest swing factor in the report after the coal price itself.

The equity bridge subtracts net debt and minority interests and adds back the non-current investments, which is where the associate's carrying value sits, so the associate is not lost inside the single-segment consolidation. That add-back is not free money and we test it. The audited carrying value of the forty-nine per cent associate was US$25.4m at the FY2025 audited date and US$24.3m at the latest balance sheet, which is the figure the bridge adds, after a year in which the associate produced nothing at all [S3] [S4]. Its own net assets are US$31.1m, so the group carries the stake at a premium to its share of the associate's book; a prudent impairment towards the associate's own equity would take a few tens of rupiah a share off the target, and the associate's licence expiry is the trigger we would watch for. We do not book that write-down in the base case, because the associate is still cash-generative when it operates and it paid the group a dividend last year [S3], but the bridge item is the softest part of the equity value and we say so.

The cross-checks disagree with the primary, and we say so. The dividend-capacity method values the name well above the DCF (Rp573, 316.2% above the primary), because it capitalises the modelled dividend at the low peer-median yield the coal names carry [S2]. We keep it because the coal card requires a dividend-capacity anchor and because the payout behind it is the stated policy midpoint, not a guess: the company's own dividend policy is a fixed share of net profit within a band, and it has paid above that band when cash allowed [S2]. But we are clear about its limits — it is a capacity anchor, it rests on a payout the company has not paid for two years, and a reader who thinks the board keeps the dividend at zero should take the DCF, not this method, as the value. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is absent for a dull reason, and round one got it wrong: it drops out because the data pack's trailing period carries no EBITDA field, so the metric cannot be computed at all — not because the metric is negative. The model's own forward EBITDA is positive in every year and the shares trade on 17.4x of forecast EBITDA, which is itself a warning about the price, but it is not the reason this method is missing [S0].

On realisation the method is deliberate rather than inherited. The calibrated ratio keys off the seaborne Newcastle marker because that is the reviewed series the whole coal peer set in this book uses and the low-rank index markers are not reviewable in the deck; the rank discount sits inside the calibrated ratio, cross-checked against the deck's own mid- and low-calorie reference prices for this rank [d.coal.newc] [d.coal.hba_ii]. Sensitivity to the benchmark price and to the rupiah is wide, and the bear and bull outcomes span a very large range, which is the honest shape of a marginal mine whose cash margin is a small residual

What the price implies is the most useful number in this report. To justify today's price on our own DCF, the seaborne benchmark would have to run at a multiple of the deck's forward path US$324/t 2.7. That is a statement about the war premium persisting, not about this company's execution. On the trailing multiples the shares have changed hands on a triple-digit multiple of trailing earnings and on a low-double-digit multiple of book 152.6x 19.2x, with the forward multiple only coming down sharply if the deck's current-year price and a volume recovery land together 26.9x.

The clearest way to lose money here on the long side is to be right about coal and wrong about this company. The realised price is a fraction of the benchmark, so a strong benchmark lifts a small absolute margin; the haul, barge and jetty charges are largely fixed per tonne, so a volume shortfall spreads them over fewer tonnes; and the annual quota is set by the government, not by the company. A downward revision to the RKAB, a further multi-year delay in the associate's restart, or a prolonged wet season that closes the haul road would each compress the margin well before the seaborne price moved [S2] [S6]. The licence clock is a risk in its own right: the producing mine's permit runs out at the end of the decade and the associate's already has, and our base value stops when the permit does [S2].

Regulatory risk is the highest-impact item: royalty rates, the domestic market obligation, export proceeds retention and quota administration are all live policy levers, and they bite hardest on the marginal producer. Macro risk is second: the deck itself flags that spot sits well above its forward path as a war-premium carry, so a normalisation of that premium is a direct hit to the value we underwrite to. Currency risk is modest and runs the other way: the company earns in dollars and reports in dollars, so a weaker rupiah flatters the rupiah share price without changing the economics. Operational risk centres on the single haul road and the single river terminal. Governance risk is real and specific — revenue concentration in a related party, a controlling shareholder above two-thirds of the register, a very small free float and a controlling stake that makes the tape thin and volatile, as the suspension showed. Liquidity risk for us is minimal: the name trades a large enough daily value to enter and exit.

Bear case — the benchmark mean-reverts faster than the deck as Chinese output restarts and Indonesian supply returns, and the quota plus a soft first half leave volume a little light. Free cash flow thins further, neither the shareholder loan nor the short-term bank loan is repaid and the dividend stays at zero; the associate stays idle as its licence runs out and its carrying value is written down; and the logistics build delivers no cost relief. Base case — the deck path is broadly right: the benchmark steps down through the middle of the decade to its long-run level, volume recovers modestly from the current run-rate, the mine runs to the end of its licence with no renewal booked, and it generates a thin but positive cash margin with the dividend at the policy midpoint. Bull case — the war premium holds, the Indonesian supply-discipline bid keeps the benchmark above the deck, the quota is lifted toward the company's own plan, the producing mine's licence is renewed into the next decade, the associate restarts, and the haul road and jetty build takes cost out of the largest line in the P&L, so volume, realised price and margin rise together and the value re-rates. Probabilities are set at the house default with the base case above 0.5.

Signposts that would change our view: an RKAB quota materially above the current run-rate; a renewal of the producing mine's operating licence past the end of the decade, which would let us extend the DCF; a restart date for the associate's East Kalimantan mine; evidence that the logistics build is taking cost out of the haulage line per tonne; a sustained benchmark above the deck's forward path for more than a quarter; and any step-change in the related-party share of revenue.

The register is concentrated and the float is thin. The controlling shareholder is a holding company of a Singapore-listed coal group that became the controlling shareholder in this century's twenties, and the ultimate beneficial owners are named individuals; the second-largest holder is an affiliated entity, and public shareholders hold a low-double-digit share 11.6 88.4 [S2]. Members of the board hold no direct shares but hold indirect interests through the controlling structure [S2]. Two corporate actions in the last audited year are structure flags under the house earnings-quality screen, and round one mentioned them without assessing them. First, the company issued 275 m sharesm new shares without pre-emptive rights for Rp220 IDR bnbn — an implied price of roughly a quarter of today's Rp3,280 — which is dilutive to public holders as a matter of arithmetic even though it was disclosed and approved [S2]. Second, it paid US$41.3m in cash for a hundred per cent of an intermediate holding company, PT Bara Enim Sejahtera, whose disclosed total assets at the year-end were a fraction of that price [S3] [S2]. The counterparty, PT Sinar Unggul Internasional, is not among the related parties the notes list, so we do not call it a related-party deal [S3]; but the price paid over the acquired book, funded partly by a placement struck far below the current market, is exactly the per-share-value-leak pattern the screen looks for, and we say so rather than bury it. Neither flag changes the rating on its own; both are reasons to hold the governance discount we already apply.

Related-party gravity is the central governance fact and the reason we would discount any related-party-derived revenue in a stress case. A very large share of the group's coal revenue is a sale to a single affiliate of the controlling shareholder under a coal sales and purchase agreement, with a marketing-services agreement alongside it, and the counterparty also holds the contract liability that funds part of the working capital 77.4 USD m [S3]. The borrowings are a related-party shareholder loan, which the group both borrows from and services inside the family of companies, plus a short-term bank loan of US$11.0m first drawn in the first half of 2026 (27.3 USD m and 11.0 USD m) [S3] [S4]. This is the modal Indonesian value-destruction channel, and while the arrangement is disclosed and carries no adverse finding, it means the realised price we calibrate to is itself a related-party price, which is a limitation on our evidence we state plainly.

The audit is clean and by a firm within a global network; the opinion is unqualified; there is no going-concern paragraph; and the only sanction disclosed is a nominal administrative penalty for a late auditor appointment in an earlier year [S2] [S3]. There is no material litigation, no special-monitoring-board status and no special-notation letter, so the IDX regime gate is clear [S2].

On the dividend record the company paid nothing in either of the last two audited years, having paid interim dividends earlier in the decade; the stated policy is a fixed share of net profit after tax within a band, subject to the general meeting, so dividend capacity exists but has not recently been exercised [S2]. On ESG, the exposures that matter are the energy transition — which management itself names as its central challenge and to which it responds with fleet electrification and operational efficiency rather than any change in the product — plus mine rehabilitation, acid mine drainage and mine-closure provisioning, all of which are disclosed and provisioned in the accounts [S2] [S3].

The dated catalysts are the quarterly filings, the annual quota decision and the audited statements. The next quarterly report is the first hard read on whether the volume recovery after the late quota issuance is real, and the quota decision for the coming year sets the volume ceiling under which the whole plan operates [S3] [S6]. The audited statements will test the company's own revenue target against what was actually realised — a test the annual report itself answers inconsistently for the last audited year, reporting the revenue plan met at about half in one section while its structured target table shows the volume target reached [S2] — so the printed actual is the number we watch, not the achievement percentage in the prose.

Between updates we watch a short list of KPIs: the realised price per tonne against the low-calorie reference series; the RKAB quota and any revision; the split of sales between export and domestic, since the domestic mix caps the price; the related-party share of revenue; the haulage cost per tonne, which is the single largest cost line; the strip ratio and overburden volume; the capex-versus-development split, so we can tell when the terminal build is finished; and the debt structure at the latest balance sheet, where the shareholder loan and a first short-term bank loan sit together, the shareholder loan being the larger and the family-serviced line [S3] [S4] [S2].

Our monitoring is deliberately built around the physical bottlenecks rather than around the coal
price alone, because for a producer of this rank the price is a market fact and the logistics are a
company fact. The two things that would make us revisit the rating upward are a sustained rise in
the realised price relative to the benchmark and evidence that the terminal build is complete, either
of which would raise the cash margin without needing us to change our view of the cycle.

bear.narrative: Newcastle mean-reverts faster than the deck as China restarts and Indonesian RKAB supply returns, and the RKAB quota plus a soft H1 leave Triaryani volume 5% light: FCF thins, the shareholder loan is not repaid and the dividend stays at zero. IPC stays idle while its IUP runs out and the associate carrying value is written down, and the MBJ haul-road/jetty build delivers no unit-cost relief.

bull.narrative: The war-premium bid holds and the Indonesian supply-discipline bid keeps Newcastle above the deck path, while the RKAB is lifted and Triaryani's logistics allow 5% more tonnes: EBITDA and dividend capacity step up well ahead of the deck. Three things the base case leaves out land together: the associate IPC restarts (it sold ~1 Mt two years ago [S2 p.81]), the Triaryani IUP is renewed past 2030 (worth ~314 Mt of reserve [S2 p.82]), and the MBJ haul road/jetty build takes cost out of the US$18.70/t haulage line [S3 note 28].

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Consolidated (PT Triaryani) sales tonnes, the base the consolidated P&L is built on. FY2026E is anchored on HARD print, not on a plan-achievement ratio: H1-2026 group sales were 1.28 Mt with no production at all from the associate IPC [S6 p.10, p.11], so a full year on the H1 run-rate is ~2.6 Mt and a modest H2 recovery after the late-March RKAB issue takes it to 2.7 Mt [S6]. This is what the engine's life-DCF carries. ROUND-1 CAVEAT, now corrected (review C1): the round-1 basis justified the haircut against the plan with a claim that the plan 'has been met at only ~60-65% in each published year [S2 p.96, p.172]'. That is half right and half mis-cited. S2 p.96 does say the 2025 production plan was met at 65.02% against the target set at the start of the year (F33), but S2 p.172's POJK target table (F2, F32) carries a 2025 TARGET column of 2,500,000 t for Triaryani against 2,569,381 t actual, i.e. the target was MET, and the F1/F2 locator mislabelled that 2025 Target column as the '2024 target'. The two figures are inconsistent inside one document, so we do not lean on plan-achievement at all: the FY2026 volume level rests on the H1-2026 actual, which caps the year well below the company's 5.5 Mt plan whatever the 2025 achievement rate was. FY2027E-30E steps up only to 3.0 Mt, inside the logistics capacity the company describes [S2 p.99] and below the FY2025 group actual of 3.26 Mt [S2 p.81].

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual, not a forecast year: FY2025A consolidated ASP US$40.33/t (revenue US$103.62m over PT Triaryani sales 2.569 Mt [S2 p.172, S3]) divided by the FY2025A Newcastle 6,000 NAR average US$108.4/t [d.coal.newc] = 0.372. The ratio absorbs Triaryani's 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR grade and its FOB/road-haul delivery point, and it cross-checks against the H1-2026 ASP of ~US$48/t [S4, S6]. Held flat: the benchmark deck carries the price path. Benchmark choice (review C12): we key on d.coal.newc because it is the industry config's price_driver for the whole COAL peer set, it carries a 20-year reviewed history, and the low-rank ICI markers (deck ici4/ici3) are not reviewable in the deck. The ratio is calibrated on the actual, so the rank discount is inside it, not assumed. Cross-check against the HBA/ICI ladder for this rank: at spot Newcastle (d.coal.newc.spot US$150.3/t) the 0.372 ratio prices Triaryani at ~US$56/t, which sits between the deck's HBA II marker (US$66.1/t) and HBA III (US$45.5/t) - the right place for a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product - even though the company itself attributes its September re-rating to the ICI reference price rather than Newcastle [S6 p.16]. We take that as a deliberate, sourced choice on the reviewed series.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; the US$70/t DMO cap sits above SMMT's realised price, so a capped share has no effect on the blended ASP at this price level [d.coal.dmo_cap].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne)
assumptions.basis: FY2025A overburden removed 7,130,388 BCM [S2 p.20] over PT Triaryani production 2,499,701 t [S2 p.172] = 2.85 bcm/t; held at the last actual because no mine plan in the filing shows grade or stripping drift, so none is modelled.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm
assumptions.basis: FY2025A overburden removal expense US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28] over 7,130,388 BCM removed [S2 p.20] = US$1.15/bcm; held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK, not left at the template default (review C13). The term scales the mining block (strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm, i.e. the overburden charge), so fuel is taken as its share of that block: fuel US$337,850 [S3 note 28, F26] over the overburden charge US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28, F11] = 4.1%. Fuel is 0.37% of the US$90.4m total production cost, so the round-1 0.3 default overstated the group's oil exposure roughly sevenfold; a real Brent move now barely moves unit cost.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, jetty, process)
assumptions.basis: FY2025A cash cost ex-royalty and ex-D&A: cost of sales US$95.23m less government royalty US$8.15m less D&A US$5.43m less overburden US$8.18m = US$73.47m, over 2.569 Mt = US$28.59/t [S3 note 28, S2 p.172]. This is the road-haul/barge/jetty/transshipment block, which dominates the cost base; held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: The effective rate the LK shows being paid: government royalty US$8,148,886 on FY2025 sales US$103,617,931 = 7.86% (FY2024: US$3,987,555 on US$51,361,902 = 7.76%), stable across both years, so 7.86% is held flat for the forecast [S3 note 28]. Under PP 19/2025 the IUP open-pit schedule for the 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche is 5%/6%/9% by HBA band, which brackets rather than matches the paid rate; the LK rate is used per the house rule that the rate paid governs.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the group reports a single coal-mining segment with no other revenue line [S3 note 35].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit
assumptions.basis: FY2025A D&A charged to cost of sales US$5,433,053 [S3 note 28] over 2.569 Mt = US$2.11/t; the data pack's US$0.16m is the direct-method cash-flow artefact and is restated from the LK. Held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex is taken at the D&A rate, US$2.11/t, because FY2025's US$10.02m of capex is a mine-development programme rather than a sustaining rate: additions to the stripping activity asset US$6.63m, exploration and evaluation US$1.70m, mining properties US$0.33m and PPE US$1.37m [S3 investing section]. The road/jetty build is a one-off, so carrying the FY2025 level forever would overstate steady-state spend. Reconciling with the falling D&A series (review C11): the P&L charge fell from US$10.48m (FY2024, F8) to US$5.43m (FY2025, F7) as the stripping and exploration additions were completed - the notes do not explain the step, so the D&A rate is a proxy, and we flag it as the softest number in the cost build. GROWTH CAPITAL: the modelled 2.57->3.0 Mt step needs no new plant - the company's own strategy is to raise the RKAB target inside the existing logistics capacity [S2 p.99] - and the incremental capital actually spent on the haul road, jetty and ports is the advance to MBJ, which sits in other non-current assets, not in the capex line [S3 note 17]. So the volume step is achieved on fleet and RKAB, not on a new mine; if the FY2025 development rate (US$3.90/t, F: FY2025 capex/FY2025 volume) were the true sustaining rate instead, free cash flow would thin further in every forecast year.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: 2025 capex was routine infrastructure, with no large expansion commitment outstanding [S2 p.94].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A, sourced to the data pack

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A effective rate; the LK books income tax net at US$2,104,771 on PBT US$6,178,631, i.e. 34% in FY2025 before the mining final-tax charge inside opex [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: borrowings are the related-party shareholder loans (US$27.29m at FY2025) [S3 note 21] plus a US$11.0m short-term bank loan drawn in H1-2026 [S4 p.5]; the engine default of 3% is consistent with the US$840,270 FY2025 interest charge [S3].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A over the data pack

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: no new facilities are committed, and FY2026 repayment of the shareholder loan is not guided [S2].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A; minorities are immaterial (0.2% of equity at FY2025) [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated dividend policy is a 15%-30% payout of net profit after tax [S2 p.101]; 25% is the policy midpoint and the most-likely forward anchor, not a cautious one (review C10). Track record is mixed but not hostile: the company paid nothing in FY2024 and FY2025 [S2 p.101], yet it paid a first interim cash dividend of Rp37/share at a 72% payout in FY2023 when cash allowed [S2 p.101], above the policy band, so it pays when it can. The FY2026E modelled year carries free cash flow of US$30.1m and builds net cash, so the 25% is fundable; the model uses it as the normalised rate rather than the zero of a capex-heavy year. The dividend yield cross-check is still run as a capacity anchor, and we note it sits far above the primary DCF - see the report.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the 2025 private placement of 275m shares is complete and no further issue is guided [S2 p.102].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: house long-run USD inflation (macro deck inflation_usd_lt 2.0%) applied to the cross-check DCF; the primary dcf_life carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last actual: FY2025 general, administrative and selling expense US$3,461,685 plus the mining final-tax charge inside the pack's opex line = US$4,102,146 on revenue US$103,617,931 = 3.96% [S3]. The three-year average (5.65%) is inflated by the thin FY2023 revenue base.

challenges.challenge: The ~45% volume haircut (FY2026E 2.7 Mt vs the company's 5.5 Mt plan) rests on the claim that 'the plan has been met at only ~60-65% in each published year [S2 p.96, p.172]'. p.96 does state 65.02% of production target, but p.172's own 2025 Target column shows PT Triaryani production target 2,500,000 t against 2,499,701 t actual (100%) and group 2,914,131 t against 3,168,039 t actual (109%), and S2 p.30 says output 'generally achieved the target'. The cited sources contradict each other and the analyst picked the bearish reading; the F1/F2 locator also labels p.172's 2025 Target column as the '2024 target'.
challenges.answer: Answered on the record. The red team is right on the locator: the PDF layout of S2 p.172 puts four columns under the year row (2025 Realisasi / 2025 TARGET / 2024 Realisasi / 2023 Realisasi), so the second column is the 2025 Target it names - Triaryani 2,500,000 t vs 2,569,381 t actually sold and group 2,914,131 t vs 3,168,039 t - and the round-1 F1/F2/F3 locators calling it the '2024 target' are corrected. The two 2025 target figures inside the one annual report do conflict: p.96 states the production plan met at 65.02% of the year-start target (F33) while p.172's structured table shows the same year's target reached (F1, F32). Because the document contradicts itself we stop leaning on plan-achievement at all: the plan-met premise sentence is deleted and the FY2026E volume level (2.7 Mt) now rests on hard print - H1-2026 sales of 1.28 Mt with no associate production and a work-plan quota issued only at end-March [S4, S6] - which caps FY2026 far below the 5.5 Mt plan whatever the 2025 achievement rate was. Volume level unchanged; the sourcing and the locators are rebuilt around the 100-109% reading.

challenges.challenge: The primary dcf_life discounts 20 years to FY2045E, but Triaryani's IUP Operasi Produksi expires in 2030 and IPC's in 2026 [S2 p.52, p.82]. Cash flows after FY2030E carry ~31% of DCF EV (cum PV 30.38 of 44.17). The horizon.reserves justification cites that 2030 expiry as the reason the DCF 'stops at the visibility window' — which is the opposite of what a 20-year cut does — and no source supports 15 years of post-licence renewal.
challenges.answer: Accepted and fixed in the model. params.horizon is cut from 20 to 5 so the primary life DCF discounts FY2026E-FY2030E only - the licensed window - instead of running 15 years past the licence to FY2045E. The licence facts are sourced: PT Triaryani's IUP Operasi Produksi expires in 2030, PT Internasional Prima Coal's in 2026 [S2 p.52, p.53, p.82]. The filing carries no renewal or extension term, so post-licence cash is not booked in base NAV; the 314 Mt reserve [S2 p.82, F5] is carried as an option in the bull case, the way the house treats exploration upside. The horizon.reserves justification is rewritten to be consistent with the 2030/2026 expiry it cites (the round-1 version cited the expiry to justify the opposite - a 20-year cut). Effect: the DCF value falls and the target moves down; the rated call is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The report says the EV/EBITDA cross-check 'drops out of the blend entirely because the metric is negative on a forward year, which is itself a signal about the margin'. The model's EBITDA is positive in every forecast year (FY2026E 34.21m, FY2027E 18.84m, ... FY2045E 11.15m) and its own FY2026E EV/EBITDA is +17.9x. The method actually drops because the datapack's LTM has no ebitda field (cov_engine.m_multiple: metric None).
challenges.answer: Accepted. The stated reason was wrong and is corrected in section 4. The EV/EBITDA cross-check drops out because the data pack's trailing period carries no EBITDA field, so the metric cannot be computed (cov_engine m_multiple returns 'metric unavailable'), not because it is negative: the model's EBITDA is positive in every forecast year and the shares trade on +17.9x FY2026E EV/EBITDA. The 'signal about the margin' sentence is deleted. The report now says the forward multiple is itself a warning about the price, but not the reason the method is absent [S0]. The method stays dropped; the explanatory text now matches the model.

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call qc_justification asserts 'the market's 70x FY2025 P/E and 8.9x P/B on a 4% net margin'. The report's own resolved multiples at the Rp3,280 price date are 152.6x FY2025A P/E and 19.2x P/B (model multiples.FY2025A). The justification's figures correspond to a price of roughly Rp1,500 — a stale pre-spike print — so the load-bearing justification for clearing a BLOCK flag is not the number the report publishes.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The extreme_call qc_justification is re-derived from the current model and price. At the Rp3,280 price date the resolved multiples are 152.6x FY2025A P/E and 19.2x P/B (model multiples.FY2025A), with FY2026E EV/EBITDA at 17.9x - the stale '70x P/E and 8.9x P/B' figures (a ~Rp1,500 print) are removed. The three sourced drivers are unchanged; the reverse-DCF factor is corrected to ~2.7x (see QC Q1) so the clearance rests on figures that match the rendered report [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report and assumptions call PT Internasional Prima Coal a 'dormant second mine' / 'dormant associate'. It is an operating 4,700-5,500 GAR IUP mine: 668,338 t produced and 690,909 t sold in FY2025 (999,983 t / 997,941 t in FY2024) [S2 p.81], and it paid the group US$2,123,285 of cash dividends in FY2025 [S3 p.14]. It is idle only in 2026 (no production per [S6 p.10]). The base case values it at book only and no bull scenario carries its restart tonnage.
challenges.answer: Accepted. PT Internasional Prima Coal is restated as an idle-capable operating mine, not a dormant one: it produced 668,338 t and sold 690,909 t in FY2025 (about 1 Mt in FY2024), is a 4,700-5,500 GAR mine with its own haul road and barging ports, and paid the group US$2.12m of cash dividends in FY2025 [S2 p.81/p.82, S3 note 11 and p.14]. Facts F20/F21/F22 added and the 'dormant' language is gone from the report and the assumptions. On valuation we take the second limb of the required answer and explain why: the base case carries the associate at its audited book value only, because it produced nothing in 2026 and the notes give no restart value, and its restart is a sourced element of the bull-case narrative rather than base NAV.

challenges.challenge: Haulage is the largest cost line (US$48,039,420, 46% of revenue, US$18.70/t [S3 note 28]) on a ~140 km road haul, and the company has been spending the FY2025 development capex on the Lalan river terminal and barge ports to relieve it. The model holds other_cost_unit at US$28.59/t for the whole 20 years, so none of the logistic investment that the report itself describes converts into unit-cost relief or volume — the upside of the capex is excluded while its downside (removed from sustaining capex) is included.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part, with the required explicit statement. The base case assumes NO unit-cost benefit from the logistics build: other_cost_unit is held at the last actual (US$28.59/t) for the whole horizon because no source in the filing quantifies the per-tonne relief the road/jetty build can deliver, and inventing one would be an unsourced haircut. What is sourced is the build itself and its funding: the company has a cooperation agreement with its affiliate PT Marga Bara Jaya to develop and operate integrated road and jetty infrastructure, targeted for completion mid-2026, and the group funds it through advances booked as other non-current assets with phased access to the capacity [S2 p.31, p.39, S3 note 17]. That upside is carried in the bull-case narrative. So the asymmetry the red team flagged - capex downside in, cost relief out - is now explicit rather than silent, and it is conservative.

challenges.challenge: EARNINGS_QUALITY item 4 requires related-party flows quantified on both sides. The report quantifies revenue (US$77.4m, 75% of sales to GCI [S3 notes 27, 34]) but not the cost side: the haul road, jetty and loading infrastructure is accessed through advances to PT Marga Bara Jaya, a related party [S3 note 17, note 34], so the US$48.0m haulage and US$8.0m jetty blocks are largely intra-group. The reader is given no measure of how much of the cost base is set by a related party.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The cost side of related-party gravity is now quantified in sections 2 and 3. On the LK's own cost-of-sales split, hauling is US$48.04m and jetty/loading US$7.99m - together the majority of cost of sales - and the haul road and jetty are provided by PT Marga Bara Jaya, an affiliate of the same controlling group, with the group funding the build via advances [S3 note 28, note 17, note 34]. The sales-side fee the same group charges is the marketing-services fee of US$1.84m (under a dollar a tonne of realised price) [S3 note 29, note 34]. We are also precise about a limit the challenge assumes away: the notes do not name the counterparty of the haulage line itself, and the only supplier disclosed above a tenth of sales is a third party (PT Ashindo Bara Perkasa), so the exposure is real but cannot be sized to the last dollar. A board member is the president director of that affiliate, which we note as governance [S2]. Facts F23/F24/F25 added.

challenges.challenge: Structure flags under EARNINGS_QUALITY item 5 are not assessed. The Company issued 275m new shares non-preemptively in April 2025 at Rp800/share (Rp220bn) [S2 p.38] — a quarter of today's Rp3,280 price — and completed a Rp673.2bn acquisition of 100% of PT Bara Enim Sejahtera from PT Sinar Unggul Internasional in July 2025 [S2 p.25, p.38]. The report mentions the placement and the holding-chain restructure but never the placement price versus market, the counterparty, or the acquisition terms.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Both corporate actions are now assessed, not just mentioned. Placement: 275m new shares issued without pre-emptive rights for Rp220bn, an implied price of roughly a quarter of today's Rp3,280, dilutive to public holders as a matter of arithmetic though disclosed and approved [S2 p.24/p.25]. Acquisition: US$41.28m in cash for 100% of PT Bara Enim Sejahtera, an intermediate holding company, from PT Sinar Unggul Internasional; SUI is NOT among the related parties the notes list (GER, GEI, IPC, MBJ, GCI, SDJ, TBR, GEC), so we do not call it a related-party deal, but the price paid runs well over the acquired entity's disclosed assets and was part-funded by the deeply discounted placement [S3 p.16, S2 p.25]. Both are now stated as structure flags feeding the governance discount; neither alone changes the rating. Facts F27/F28/F29 added.

challenges.challenge: The DCF equity bridge adds back 'investments' of US$24.297m — 63% of the US$38.56m DCF equity value — as the associate's carrying value [S3 p.10, p.48: US$25,407,070 at 31 Dec 2025], with no fact, source or impairment test. IPC's IUP expired in 2026 and it produced nothing in 2026, yet the model carries the full book value into the target.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The associate carrying value is now a sourced fact with a locator - F19, US$25,407,070 at 31 Dec 2025, S3 note 11 / p.10 - and the equity bridge item is tied to it. The report states the impairment test explicitly and its direction: the group carries the 49% stake at US$25.41m against a 49% share of the associate's own US$31.14m of net assets (F30), so the stake is carried above its share of the associate's book and a write-down, not a write-up, is the risk. We do not book the write-down in the base case, because the associate is cash-generative when it operates and paid a dividend last year, but we name the licence expiry as the trigger and flag the bridge as the softest part of equity value [S3].

challenges.challenge: The div_yield cross-check is worth Rp554 on a 20% weight and lifts the base target from the DCF's Rp204 to Rp273. It is built on a 25% payout [S2 p.101 policy midpoint], yet the company paid no dividend in FY2024 or FY2025 and is funding a capex programme; the pack's dps_ttm is zero. A cross-check this far above the primary, resting on a payout never yet paid, is unjustified optimism that understates how bearish the base case is.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part. We take the first limb of the required answer - justify the payout with a source - rather than cutting it, because the midpoint is the most-likely rate, not the cautious one. The 25% is the midpoint of the company's own stated 15%-30% policy band [S2 p.101], the company paid a first interim dividend at a 72% payout in FY2023 when cash allowed (above the band) [S2 p.101], and the FY2026E modelled year carries free cash flow of US$30.1m and builds net cash, so the rate is fundable. What we fix is the presentation: section 4 now states plainly that the dividend-capacity cross-check sits far above the primary, explains WHY (it capitalises the modelled dividend at the low peer-median coal yield), and tells the reader who expects a zero payout to take the DCF, not this method, as the value. The payout assumption is unchanged; the divergence is now disclosed with its limits rather than left to lift the target silently.

challenges.challenge: Sustaining capex is cut from FY2025's US$10.02m (US$3.90/t) to the D&A rate of US$2.11/t (FY2026E US$5.70m) while the model grows volume from 2.57 to 3.0 Mt. The FY2025 spend is excused as a development programme, but no sourced mine plan shows the growth capex needed to take a 2.5 Mt operation to 3.0 Mt, and D&A halved year-on-year (FY2024 US$10.48m to FY2025 US$5.43m [S3 note 28]), so it is not obviously the steady-state rate.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The sustaining-capex rate is reconciled rather than asserted. We keep capex at the D&A rate (US$2.11/t) and say why, and we flag the soft spot: the P&L depreciation that sets that rate fell from US$10.48m to US$5.43m between the last two audited years with no explanation in the notes, so the rate is a proxy, not a mine plan [S3 note 28, F7/F8]. On the growth capital the volume step needs: none of the sort implied - the company's own strategy is to raise the output target inside the existing logistics capacity [S2 p.99], so the incremental 2.57->3.0 Mt rides on fleet and the annual quota rather than on a new mine, and the capital actually spent on the haul road, jetty and ports sits as an advance to the logistics affiliate in other non-current assets, not in the capex line [S3 note 17]. We state in the report that if the FY2025 development rate were the true steady-state rate FCF would thin further, i.e. our assumption is the more generous reading.

challenges.challenge: The COAL card (step 4) says coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle, and the company itself attributes the September re-rating to the ICI reference price [S6 p.16]. The model calibrates 0.372 against Newcastle and holds it flat for 20 years; the low-rank HBA/ICI markers (HBA II spot US$66.1, HBA III US$45.53) bracket the realised US$40.33/t differently from Newcastle (108.4), so the choice is material.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The realisation basis now carries the HBA/ICI cross-check the challenge asks for, and states that the Newcastle basis is a deliberate, sourced choice. Cross-check: at spot Newcastle (US$150.3/t) the calibrated 0.372 ratio prices Triaryani at about US$56/t, which sits between the deck's HBA II marker (US$66.1/t) and HBA III (US$45.5/t) - the right place for a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product. Deliberate choice: we key on d.coal.newc because it is the industry config's price_driver for the entire COAL peer set, it carries the reviewed 20-year history, and the low-rank index markers (ici4/ici3) are not reviewable in the deck. The rank discount is inside the ratio, which is calibrated on the actual, not assumed. We note the company itself attributes its September re-rating to the ICI reference price [S6 p.16] and accept the Newcastle basis as the reviewed proxy.

challenges.challenge: fuel_share is left at the engine template default of 0.3 — i.e. 30% of the mining-cost block escalates with Brent — while the LK shows fuel is US$337,850 of a US$90.4m production cost (0.37%) [S3 note 28].
